title: And Am I Born to Die
description: And Am I Born to Die in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 43.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: And am I born to die? To lay this bo-dy down? And must my trem-bling spir-it_ fly In-to a world un-known A land of deep-est shade, Un-pierced by hu-man thought, The drea-ry re-gions of the dead, Where all things are for-got?

lines: And am I born to die?
And must my trembling spirit fly
The dreary regions of the dead,
Soon as from earth I go,
I from my grave shall rise,
And see the Judge with glory crowned,
How shall I leave my tomb?
A fearful or a joyful doom,
Or devils drag my soul away,
Shall I be with the damned cast out,
I must from God be driven,
Must come at his command to heaven,
O thou that wouldst not have
Who died'st thyself; my soul to save
Show me the way to shun
That when thou comest on thy throne
So shall I spend my life's short day
So shall I love my God,
And praise thee in thy bright abode,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
